propositions.claim: The order was printed in Public Health Reports, a Public Health Service periodical, on 12 Oct 1917, signed Woodrow Wilson, The White House, September 27, 1917.
propositions.quote: QUARANTINE SERVICE IN THE VIRGIN ISLANDS. EXECUTIVE ORDER PLACING THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE QUARANTINE SERVICE UNDER THE PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICE.

propositions.claim: The order extends the 1893 quarantine act and the Treasury rules under it to the three islands.
propositions.quote: all rules and regulations heretofore prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury under this act are to be given full force and effect in the islands of St. Thomas, St. Croix, and St. John

propositions.claim: The order itself takes the quarantine property of the former government, a one-time act completed by the order's own words.
propositions.quote: quarantine reservations, buildings, wharves, docks connected therewith, and equipment, be, and hereby are, taken for uses and purposes of the United States

propositions.claim: The order charges the Secretary of the Treasury, through the Surgeon General, with administering the quarantine service.
propositions.quote: the Secretary of the Treasury, through the Surgeon General of the Public Health Service, is hereby charged with all administrative duties relating to said quarantine service

propositions.claim: The order directs estimates to be prepared and submitted to Congress. Performance is not shown.
propositions.quote: shall have estimates prepared by the Surgeon General of the Public Health Service and submitted to Congress for an appropriation for the maintenance of said quarantine service

propositions.claim: Candidate ending for c1: the U.S. Code records 42 U.S.C. 92 to 96 as repealed in 1944. That range is mixed: the notes on the page attribute sections 92, 93 and 94 to the 1893 act (secs. 3, 4, 5), section 95 to an 1890 act and section 96 to a 1906 act. The repeal note does not name the order, so it is a candidate only.
propositions.quote: §§ 92 to 96. Repealed. July 1, 1944, ch. 373, title XIII, § 1313, 58 Stat. 714

propositions.claim: The repealed section 92 was the 1893 act's provision for enforcing quarantine regulations, now covered by 42 U.S.C. 264-267.
propositions.quote: Section 92, acts Feb. 15, 1893, ch. 114, §3, 27 Stat. 450; ... provided for enforcement of quarantine regulations. See sections 264 to 267 of this title.

propositions.claim: Candidate ending for c3: Treasury's public health functions were transferred to the Federal Security Agency in 1939; the note does not name the order.
propositions.quote: Functions of Department of the Treasury relating to public health transferred to Federal Security Agency pursuant to Reorg. Plan No. I of 1939

propositions.claim: The held compilation text agrees with the official printing in the operative words; it reads '1906' where Public Health Reports prints '1916' for the recited act.
propositions.quote: Whereas, an Act of Congress approved June 19, 1906, provides “that the Secretary of the Treasury shall have the control, direction, and management of all quarantine stations

propositions.claim: A quarantine-station act of June 19, 1906 (ch. 3433, 34 Stat. 300-301) exists, which is consistent with the held text's '1906' reading of the recital. The cited page shows only secs. 4 and 6 of that act (penalties; cession of jurisdiction), not the control-and-management provision the recital quotes, so which of '1906' and '1916' is correct is not established here. The difference is in the recital only and does not touch the operative clauses.
propositions.quote: Section 96, act June 19, 1906, ch. 3433, §6, 34 Stat. 301, provided that jurisdiction over established station acquired by the United States be ceded
propositions.where: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title42/pdf/USCODE-2023-title42-chap2.pdf (Title 42 p. 11; sec. 85 note on p. 9 cites §4 of the same act)

propositions.claim: Candidate ending for c1 (further): other codified sections of the 1893 act (secs. 1, 2, 6, 11, at 42 U.S.C. 81, 82, 83, 84) were repealed by the same 1944 provision, in a range (sections 81 to 87) that also includes sections from other acts; the note does not name the order.
propositions.quote: §§ 81 to 87. Repealed. July 1, 1944, ch. 373, title XIII, § 1313, 58 Stat. 714 Section 81, act Feb. 15, 1893, ch. 114, §1, 27 Stat. 449, provided penalties for entry of vessels in violation of quarantine laws. See section 271 of this title.

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN follows the project's evidence-gap rule: c2 was spent on issue under rule (c), while c1 and c3 lack a qualifying ending or positive cutoff-date source, and c4 lacks evidence of performance. General repeal and transfer notes cannot supply an ending under the stated rules. Formal status is upheld only as 'no express ending found in the reviewed evidence,' not proof that none exists. The basis_rule field should identify the OPEN evidence-gap rule rather than merely 'none'.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (NOT_FOUND fits the missing qualifying ending/current-status evidence; NEEDS_RULING does not). The project already bars inferring an ending from a general statute that does not name the order. The slice supplies neither a naming instrument nor current-law support, and the worker identifies an unread statute, not an unresolved project rule.
review.suspected_defect: The first gap incorrectly treats an already specified project rule as needing an owner ruling. Also, p6 overattributes a mixed statutory range to the 1893 act, and p10 presents an incompletely sourced inference as an established correction. Intent cannot be determined.

verdicts.reason: CDC's official Public Health Reports PDF, first page (1705), confirms the heading, publication date, signature and order date. https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/67797/cdc_67797_DS1.pdf
Page 1705 expressly extends both the February 15, 1893 act and previously prescribed Treasury rules to the three named islands.
Page 1705 says the specified property 'be, and hereby are, taken'; this performs the taking on September 27, 1917 and supports rule (c).
Page 1705 expressly assigns quarantine administration to Treasury through the Surgeon General.
Page 1705 directs preparation and submission of estimates, including maintenance, reservations and additional facilities. It does not establish performance.

The repeal quotation is accurate, but the attribution of sections 92–96 collectively to the 1893 act is inaccurate: section 95 derives from 1890 and section 96 from 1906; section 92a derives from 1878. The repeal remains candidate counterevidence, without naming EO 2717. Verified in the corresponding GovInfo printing, pp. 10–11: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title42/pdf/USCODE-2023-title42-chap2.pdf
The GovInfo printing, p. 10, confirms section 92's 1893 origin, enforcement subject and cross-reference to sections 264–267.
The transfer note under section 90, p. 10 of the GovInfo printing, confirms the 1939 transfer and does not name EO 2717. It establishes candidate counterevidence only.

Opened the named held text. Its operative provisions agree with the Public Health Reports printing; its recital reads 1906 while the official PDF text reads 1916. Its header identifies the Bureau of National Literature compilation.

The quoted section 96 note is present on p. 11 and identifies a 1906 quarantine-station statute, but concerns cession of jurisdiction, not the control-and-management provision quoted in the recital. The asserted correction is plausible but not conclusively established by this citation; the recited provision itself needs checking.
